column1: # Bench panel: Barrett et al. 1993 (doi:10.1006/viro.1993.1217), "universal"
# morbillivirus P-gene primers, the pair this registry holds as MorbF/MorbR.
# The PDF on disk is an image scan with no text layer; read 2026-10-20 from a
# 400 dpi tesseract OCR of its three pages, and the two primer sequences in that
# OCR match the registry base for base (the OCR renders one T as I).
# The claim: "We have identified a 'universal' morbillivirus primer set, based
# on highly conserved regions of the morbillivirus phosphoprotein (P) gene and
# used this to amplify a region surrounding the RNA editing site from all known
# members of the group" (abstract). The Methods name the six viruses whose
# amplified DNA was cloned and sequenced: "RNA purified from Vero cells infected
# with rinderpest virus (RPV), peste des petits ruminants virus (PPRV), canine
# distemper virus (CDV), phocine distemper virus (PDV), and the dolphin (DMV) and
# porpoise (PMV) morbilliviruses". Measles is the seventh row: the primer
# coordinates are given on the measles P mRNA (nt 400-419 and 808-828) and
# measles is one of the four sequences the primers were aligned from, so the
# paper treats it as amplified, though it is not in that Methods list.
# Amplicon: "a 429 nucleotide DNA fragment which spanned the RNA editing site".
# NO NEGATIVES. The paper reports no virus that failed to amplify, so this panel
# can show false fails and cannot show false detects. Same limitation as
# docs/bench-panels/rebelo-2011-mycoplasma.tsv.
# One genome per species, RefSeq where there is one. PMV has no complete genome;
# KF650727.1 is its P gene as a 429 bp partial, which is the Barrett product
# itself, so that row tests the sites that actually primed rather than a genome.
